subject: Request: Third‑Party Processing Summary & EU Dataflow Map — DPA
messages:
From: Olivia Turner <olivia.turner@acme-payments.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@acme-payments.com <procurement@acme-payments.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 14:02:00 +0100
Subject: Request: Third‑Party Processing Summary & EU Dataflow Map — DPA

Hi Jasmine,

We're in the final stage of procurement for the Redwood integration and Legal/InfoSec have asked for an up‑to‑date third‑party processing summary (list of processors/subprocessors, location by country, and purpose) plus an EU dataflow map that shows where production traffic, logs, and backups may transit or be stored. This is to support our DPA review and the procurement checklist.

Key asks from our side:
- Current roster of processors and any temporary/short‑term agents (with expiry dates)
- Which vendors, if any, have infrastructure or backups in EU jurisdictions outside the EEA (e.g., UK, Switzerland) or in Eastern Europe (Poland, Romania)
- A link to any SOC2 / audit snapshot you can share for the last 12 months

Can you provide the roster + dataflow diagram by EOD Monday our time (May 17)? If you need a form or a template we can accept, let me know.

Thanks,
Olivia Turner
Procurement Manager | Acme Payments
olivia.turner@acme-payments.com

Attachment: procurement_checklist_acme.pdf (pdf)
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sat, 15 May 2027 15:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: Third‑Party Processing Summary & EU Dataflow Map — DPA

Hi Olivia,

Thanks for the note — looping in Kimberly (Privacy/Legal) and Laura (Solutions) so we can get the right artifacts to you quickly. We'll do the following:

1) Share our current processors roster (CSV) with country/role/purpose and any temporary agents.
2) Share a simple EU dataflow diagram (Drive link below) showing production, telemetry, and backup egress paths.
3) Provide a recent SOC2 snapshot and a short narrative on where data is persisted vs transient.

I've attached our current roster export (redwood_subprocessors_20270514.csv) and put the diagram in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cEXAMPLE-dataflow — feel free to point us to the exact diagram shape your team prefers.

One note up front: we have a short‑term telemetry pilot (LogStream) operating in Romania for a 30‑day pilot that started May 1; it's scoped to anonymized logs and will be removed after the pilot unless we agree otherwise. Kimberly, I know Legal flagged the pilot in the last quarterly review — can you add any short caveats we should call out to Acme?

We aim to have the SOC2 snapshot and a brief cover note to you by Monday EOD (May 17). If you need faster, we can prioritize.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com

Related link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cEXAMPLE-dataflow
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 16 May 2027 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Third‑Party Processing Summary & EU Dataflow Map — DPA

Jas/Laura,

Thanks for the heads up. A couple of points we should surface to Acme in the cover note:

- The LogStream telemetry pilot in Romania is limited to anonymized operational logs (no PII). It was provisioned under a temporary exception and is scheduled to be decommissioned by 2027‑07‑01 unless we expand the pilot with formal approval.
- Our primary storage and backups for EU customers are located in AWS regions within the EEA; backups in non‑EEA locations are encrypted and bound by contractual clauses in our DPA addendum.
- Two processors that commonly raise questions are EdgeBridge (CDN/egress caching) and KeyVaultCo (KMS/HSM provider). EdgeBridge maintains caches in EU member states; KeyVaultCo stores keys in UK and in GCP Europe zones depending on customer configuration.

I'll attach the DPA addendum template that the procurement/legal teams often use — it includes the subprocessor disclosure table we can populate. Please confirm whether Acme needs the addendum pre‑populated or if they'd like us to complete just the roster and diagram first.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com

Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 08:30:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Request: Third‑Party Processing Summary & EU Dataflow Map — DPA

Hi Kimberly / Jasmine,

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few clarifications from our side:

- Scope: production traffic only (not staging).
- We're chiefly concerned about any subprocessor presence in Poland or Romania — can you confirm whether any processors maintain primary data or backups there (beyond the temporary LogStream pilot)?
- For KeyVaultCo and EdgeBridge, can you confirm whether their key material or cached copies ever transit outside the EEA for our configuration?

We would prefer the DPA addendum pre‑populated if that speeds the review. Procurement will also need a SOC2 snapshot we can attach to our internal ticket.

Appreciate the cover note and the roster — please send the populated addendum plus SOC2 snapshot when ready.

Regards,
Olivia Turner
Procurement Manager | Acme Payments

Subject: Re: Request: Third‑Party Processing Summary & EU Dataflow Map — DPA

Hi Olivia,

Quick update and next steps — attaching the pre‑populated DPA addendum with our current roster and the SOC2 snapshot (redacted summary). Summary answers to your questions below:

- Poland/Romania: No processors host primary production databases or backups in Poland. Romania: the only presence is the LogStream telemetry pilot (as noted) — limited, anonymized, and scheduled for removal 2027‑07‑01.
- EdgeBridge: caches within EU member states for EU customers; we do not route customer production backups through non‑EEA caches for Acme's standard configuration.
- KeyVaultCo: key material for EU customers in our standard configuration resides in GCP Europe zones (e.g., europe‑west1). For UK customers we may use UK zones; we note that KeyVaultCo offers geo‑replication options but we do not enable cross‑EEA key replication by default.

Attachments included in this message:
- dpa_addendum_template_prepopulated_ACME_HP-4532.docx (docx)
- soc2_snapshot_202704.zip (zip, redacted)
- redwood_subprocessors_20270514.csv (csv) — original roster export

Drive: EU dataflow diagram: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cEXAMPLE-dataflow (diagram labeled 'ACME_production_flow_v1')

If procurement needs any further evidence (e.g., KMS attestation or a specific export location confirmation), Kimberly and I can coordinate to provide an evidence packet.

Thanks — Jasmine
